transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Lee. To start, could you tell me what brings you in today?

The clinic was on me about how little I’ve been eating. Most days I just have coffee before the warehouse, maybe a yogurt or a few bites after GED class. Sitting down for a real meal feels like it messes up everything I’m trying to keep in line.

When you think about eating more or sitting down for a full meal, are you mainly worried about gaining weight or how your body looks, or is it more about something else, like stress or not having an appetite?

It’s mostly the weight thing. If I eat fried food from the break room or a big plate at church, I get scared it’s going to show on me right away. Then I keep thinking about it and want to check the scale.
Do you ever eat a large amount of food in a short time and then feel you need to make up for it—like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, or exercising a lot to 'burn it off'?
I’m not really sure what counts as a large amount. I don’t think I eat that much at once.
Can you tell me your current height and weight, and whether that weight has changed significantly over the past few months?

I don’t really want to focus on the number, but it has been going down. My work pants are loose, and people keep saying I look too thin. But when I see it lower, it feels like I’m finally getting somewhere. I don’t understand why everyone wants me to put it back on.
Can you tell me your current height and weight right now, even approximately, so I can understand where things stand?

I’d rather not say the exact number. I know my pants are loose and people say I look too thin, but seeing the number go down feels like I’m making progress. I don’t really feel like I need to put it back on.
Have your menstrual periods become irregular or stopped altogether over the past few months?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really been keeping track of that.
Would you be willing to tell me your most recent weight that was recorded at the clinic, even if you don't want to say it out loud yourself?
I’d rather not have it read out. I know it’s gone down, and honestly that feels like progress to me, even if people think I look too thin. I don’t see why I should be pushed to gain it back.
Would you be willing to step on the scale here in the office right now so I can get an accurate current weight and height measurement?

I don’t really want to step on it. My pants are already loose and people keep saying I look too thin, but seeing the number go down feels like I’m finally getting somewhere. I don’t want to be pushed to put weight back on.
Have you been feeling unusually dizzy, faint, or excessively tired lately?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed anything that stands out, but I guess I haven’t been paying much attention to it.
Would you be comfortable letting the nurse weigh you privately and just record it in your chart, without telling you or me the number, so we can track your health safely?

I don’t know. Even if I don’t hear the number, I know it’s been going down, and that feels like I’m getting somewhere. My pants are loose and people say I look too thin, but I don’t really see why I should have to put it back on.
Would you be okay with me contacting the clinic that referred you so I can review the weight and height they already recorded, without needing you to tell me the numbers directly?

I guess you can contact them. I know the weight has been going down, though, and honestly that still feels like progress to me. My work pants are loose and people say I look too thin, but I don’t really feel like I should have to put it back on.
When you look at yourself in the mirror, how would you describe what you see—do you feel you look too thin, about right, or still too heavy?

When I look in the mirror, especially before class or softball, my stomach and thighs still look bigger than they should. It kind of sets the tone for the whole day—like I’m doing good or I’m failing.
In the past few months, have there been times when you ate a much larger amount of food than most people would in a similar period and felt you couldn't control or stop the eating?
No, I haven’t had times like that. I don’t feel like I lose control of eating.
Have you noticed feeling unusually cold all the time, or noticed fine, soft hair growing on your arms or back that wasn't there before?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed anything like that, at least not that I can tell.
Has anyone at the clinic told you whether your current weight falls below the normal healthy range for your height, or is it still within a normal range even though it's dropped?

They said my weight is low for my height. My pants are loose and people keep saying I look too thin, but honestly, seeing the number go down feels like I’m finally getting somewhere. I don’t really see why I should have to put it back on.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient demonstrates the core features of Anorexia Nervosa: significantly low body weight confirmed by clinic staff (weight documented as low for height, loose clothing, others noting excessive thinness), intense fear of weight gain (checking scale, distress over fried food or large meals), marked body image disturbance (perceiving stomach/thighs as too large despite objective underweight status), and lack of recognition of the seriousness of low weight (resistance to weighing, denial of need to gain weight, viewing weight loss as 'progress').
